tagline: Sunset is a press release. Ghosts are a runtime.

exhibits.title: Stadia
exhibits.obituaryNote: Official goodbye: “Stadia service is no longer available. Thanks for playing.”
exhibits.note: The product is dead. The hostname still serves a 200 with the funeral already printed on the page. That is a ghost, not a 410.

exhibits.title: Google Domains
exhibits.obituaryNote: Google announced sale of domain registrations to Squarespace.
exhibits.note: The registrar was sold. The original lockup still answers on domains.google — a storefront for a product Google no longer operates.

exhibits.title: Vine
exhibits.obituaryNote: Twitter discontinued the Vine mobile apps in 2016–2017.
exhibits.note: The six-second network was killed. vine.co still returns 200 and still calls itself Vine. Do not build on it.

exhibits.title: SWFObject on Google Hosted Libraries
exhibits.obituaryNote: Adobe ended Flash Player distribution December 31, 2020.
exhibits.note: The runtime had a funeral. The loader script that embedded .swf files is still a 200 on a public CDN. A door to a room that was demolished.

exhibits.title: Azure AD Graph
exhibits.obituaryNote: Microsoft documented Azure AD Graph retirement (extended access ended 2025).
exhibits.note: Retired APIs should go 410. This host still speaks Azure AD Graph JSON: 401 invalid_token, odata.error. The door is locked. It is not gone.

exhibits.title: Mixer
exhibits.obituaryNote: Microsoft shut Mixer down in July 2020.
exhibits.titleTag: Facebook Gaming | Disfruta de streaming de videojuegos en vivo
exhibits.note: mixer.com 301s into Facebook Gaming. The name on the door is Mixer. The room is someone else’s product.

exhibits.title: Atom
exhibits.note: atom.io still answers — by walking you to its own obituary. A polite ghost.

exhibits.title: Orkut
exhibits.obituaryNote: Google announced farewell to Orkut; service shut September 30, 2014.
exhibits.note: Google bid Orkut farewell in 2014. orkut.com still returns 200 and still calls itself orkut. A social network with a decade-old funeral and a living front door.

exhibits.title: Google Code
exhibits.obituaryNote: Google shut project hosting on Google Code on January 25, 2016.
exhibits.note: Project hosting was closed in 2016. code.google.com still answers with a 200 titled Google Code — an archive door that never got a 410.

exhibits.title: Google Wave
exhibits.obituaryNote: Google announced Wave would stop being developed as a standalone product; service later ended.
exhibits.titleTag: Status of Google Wave - Google Help
exhibits.note: wave.google.com still answers — by walking you to a help article about the status of Google Wave. The name on the door is Wave. The room is the obituary.

exhibits.title: Google+
exhibits.obituaryNote: Google shut down consumer Google+ in April 2019.
exhibits.titleTag: Google Workspace Updates: New community features for Google Chat and an update on Currents
exhibits.note: plus.google.com still answers — by walking you to a Workspace blog about Chat and Currents. The name on the door is Plus. The room is the funeral program.

exhibits.title: Adobe Flash Player download
exhibits.obituaryNote: Adobe ended Flash Player distribution December 31, 2020.
exhibits.titleTag: Adobe Flash Player End of Life
exhibits.note: The download door still exists. It 301s into Adobe’s Flash end-of-life page. A storefront that only sells the obituary.

exhibits.title: Google Play Music
exhibits.obituaryNote: Google moved Play Music users to YouTube Music and shut the service down.
exhibits.note: play.google.com/music still answers — straight into YouTube Music. The old listening room opens someone else’s product.

exhibits.title: Google Allo
exhibits.obituaryNote: Google shut Allo down in March 2019.
exhibits.titleTag: Prueba Mensajes de Google y guarda lo importante
exhibits.note: allo.google.com still answers by walking into Google Messages. Another polite successor facade.

exhibits.title: AngularJS
exhibits.note: The framework’s funeral was scheduled. angularjs.org still returns 200. Docs for a runtime that was supposed to be finished.

exhibits.title: Panoramio
exhibits.obituaryNote: Google said goodbye to Panoramio in 2016.
exhibits.note: A photo network with a 2016 funeral. panoramio.com still answers 200.

exhibits.title: Polymer Project
exhibits.obituaryNote: Polymer Project pointed developers toward Lit and related successors.
exhibits.note: polymer-project.org still answers — by walking into library docs. The project name on the door; the docs of what replaced it inside.

exhibits.title: Google URL Shortener (goo.gl)
exhibits.obituaryNote: Google shut down goo.gl link creation and later limited resolution.
exhibits.note: The shortener had a funeral. goo.gl still answers — with 400 Invalid Dynamic Link, not 410. The socket speaks. It refuses. It is not gone.

exhibits.title: Parse.com API
exhibits.obituaryNote: Parse hosted service shut down January 28, 2017. Open-source Parse Server remains.
exhibits.note: Contrast hanging. Parse returns 410 with a pointer to the open-source funeral home. This is what a completed sunset looks like.
